46317-ella-clinton-or-by-their-fruits-ye.title: By Their Fruits Ye Shall Know Them.
46317-ella-clinton-or-by-their-fruits-ye.creator: Martha Farquharson,
46317-ella-clinton-or-by-their-fruits-ye.description: A book by Martha Farquharson,. "I hate Aunt Prudence! She's always scolding and slapping me. I wish _she_ was dead instead of mother. why, O why, did you die and leave me? I can't be good without you. I do try to be good, but Aunt Prudence always makes me naughty. I can't help hating her when she's so cross. come back, come back!"

51893-the-land-of-little-rain.creator: Mary Austin
51893-the-land-of-little-rain.description: A book by Mary Austin. Desert is a loose term to indicate land that supports no man; whether the land can be bitted and broken to that purpose is not proven. Void of life it never is, however dry the air and villainous the soil.

arxiv-2205-11531.title: Implications of the Zero 1-3 Flavour Mixing Hypothesis: Predictions for θ 23 PMNS \theta_{23}^{\mathrm{PMNS}} and δ PMNS \delta^{\mathrm{PMNS}}
arxiv-2205-11531.creator: Stefan Antusch, Kevin Hinze, Shaikh Saad
arxiv-2205-11531.description: Abstract We revisit mixing sum rule relations in the lepton and quark sectors under the assumption that the 1-3 elements of the flavour mixing matrices ( V L u , V L d , V L e , V L ν V^{u}_{L},V^{d}_{L},V^{e}_{L},V^{\nu}_{L} ) are zero in the flavour basis.

arxiv-2402-04932.title: Growth in the universal cover under large simplicial volume
arxiv-2402-04932.creator: Hannah Alpert
arxiv-2402-04932.description: Abstract . Consider a closed manifold M M with two Riemannian metrics: one hyperbolic metric, and one other metric g g . What hypotheses on g g guarantee that for a given radius r r , there are balls of radius r r in the universal cover of ( M , g ) (M,g) with greather-than-hyperbolic volumes?

arxiv-2410-06294.title: A New Architecture for Neural Enhanced Multiobject Tracking
arxiv-2410-06294.creator: Shaoxiu Wei, Mingchao Liang, and Florian Meyer
arxiv-2410-06294.description: Abstract Multiobject tracking (MOT) is an important task in robotics, autonomous driving, and maritime surveillance. Traditional work on MOT is model-based and aims to establish algorithms in the framework of sequential Bayesian estimation. More recent methods are fully data-driven and rely on the training of neural networks. The two approaches have demonstrated advantages in certain scenarios.

arxiv-2411-18511.title: Scaling SU(2) to 1000 GPUs using HiRep
arxiv-2411-18511.creator: Antonio Rago
arxiv-2411-18511.description: Abstract HiRep allows flexible simulations of higher representations of Wilson Fermions with various actions and gauge groups and a range of inverters and integrators. This is particularly important for enabling evaluations of observables relevant to phenomenological inputs for Beyond-the-Standard-Model physics from lattice field theory.

arxiv-2502-18482.title: MixLLM: Dynamic Routing in Mixed Large Language Models
arxiv-2502-18482.creator: Xinyuan Wang, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Xujiang Zhao, Zhengzhang Chen, Wenchao Yu, Yanjie Fu, Haifeng Chen
arxiv-2502-18482.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit potential artificial generic intelligence recently, however, their usage is costly with high response latency. Given mixed LLMs with their own strengths and weaknesses, LLM routing aims to identify the most suitable model for each query in the stream to maximize response quality and minimize cost and latency.

arxiv-2512-00747.title: Evidence for itinerant electron-local moment interaction in Li-doped α \alpha -MnTe
arxiv-2512-00747.creator: Tingjun Zhang, Steven J. Gomez Alvarado, Sijie Xu, Travis J. Williams, Xiaoping Wang, Junhong He, Matthew B. Stone, Colin Sarkis, Feng Ye, Zhaoyu Liu, Jinyulin Li, Aparna Jayakumar, Zehao Wang, Yaofeng Xie, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Pengcheng Dai
arxiv-2512-00747.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tingjun Zhang, Steven J. Gomez Alvarado, Sijie Xu, Travis J. Williams, Xiaoping Wang, Junhong He, Matthew B. Stone, Colin Sarkis, Feng Ye, Zhaoyu Liu, Jinyulin Li, Aparna Jayakumar, Zehao Wang, Yaofeng Xie, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Pengcheng Dai. We use inelastic neutron scattering to study the impact of Li doping on the semiconducting altermagnet α \alpha -MnTe. Introducing Li results in a spin reorientation from in-plane to out-of-plane and increases the density of itinerant carriers.

arxiv-2512-07153.title: A Structured Review of Fixed and Multimodal Sensing Techniques for Bat Monitoring
arxiv-2512-07153.creator: Erwei He, Sravya Ganti, Maatla Sefawe, Julianna Segalla, Isaac Tourner, Julia Gersey
arxiv-2512-07153.description: Abstract Abstract Effective monitoring of mobile animal populations is crucial for ecological research, wildlife management, and agricultural applications. Monitoring of bats specifically can help understand the spread of disease as well as shine light on bat migration patterns, population dynamics, and the impacts of environmental changes on bat colonies.

arxiv-2602-18276.title: Chromaticity-Optimized Antenna Design and Bayesian Foreground Validation for the CANTAR Global 21 cm Experiment
arxiv-2602-18276.creator: Michelle Mora, Germán Chaparro, Juan D. Guerrero, Catalina Alzate, Juan P. Urrego, Jimena Giraldo, Pablo Cuartas-Restrepo, Julian Rodriguez-Ferreira, Oscar Restrepo
arxiv-2602-18276.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Michelle Mora, Germán Chaparro, Juan D. Guerrero, Catalina Alzate, Juan P. Urrego, Jimena Giraldo, Pablo Cuartas-Restrepo, Julian Rodriguez-Ferreira, Oscar Restrepo. Detecting the global 21 cm signal from the epoch of reionization remains a major observational challenge due to bright foregrounds and instrumental systematics. As part of the Colombian Antarctic Telescopes for 21 cm Absorption during Reionization (CANTAR) initiative, we present a simulation and analysis framework to evaluate antenna chromaticity, optimize instrument design, and assess site suitability for global 21 cm experiments.

pmc-10559449.title: Self-assessment of residents in breaking bad news; skills and barriers
pmc-10559449.creator: Maryam Mansoursamaei, Atefeh Ghanbari Jolfaei, Mehdi Zandi, Ali Mansoursamaei, Razieh Salehian
pmc-10559449.description: IntroductionBreaking bad news (BBN) is inevitable in medicine and is one of the most important and difficult professional tasks of physicians. The main aims of this study are to evaluate residents’ practice of BBN and identify perceived barriers to its implementation.

pmc-11493283.title: N4-Hydroxycytidine/molnupiravir inhibits RNA virus-induced encephalitis by producing less fit mutated viruses
pmc-11493283.creator: Durbadal Ojha, Collin S. Hill, Shuntai Zhou, Alyssa Evans, Jacqueline M. Leung, Christine A. Schneider, Franck Amblard, Tyson A. Woods, Raymond F. Schinazi, Ralph S. Baric, Karin E. Peterson, Ronald Swanstrom
pmc-11493283.description: A diverse group of RNA viruses have the ability to gain access to the central nervous system (CNS) and cause severe neurological disease. Current treatment for people with this type of infection is generally limited to supportive care. To address the need for reliable antivirals, we utilized a strategy of lethal mutagenesis to limit virus replication.

pmc-11816961.title: Prevalence of health-related behaviours and associated factors in university students in Ireland: a 4-year repeated cross-sectional study
pmc-11816961.creator: Aoife Noonan, Audrey Tierney, Catherine Norton, Kwok Ng, Catherine Woods
pmc-11816961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundTransitioning to higher education (HE) has been highlighted as a critical time to embed positive health-related behaviours (HRBs). However, there has been a long-standing association between student life and risk-taking. This study aimed to (1) identify the prevalence of HRBs over time in cohorts of HE students in Ireland, (2) establish an overall health index and analyse the health-related status of HE students and associated factors based on this index and (3) explore student perspectives towards public health interventions.MethodsUsing an anonymous, repeated

pmc-12567998.title: Computed Tomography Volumetric Measurements of Adrenal Glands in 26 Dogs Under One Year of Age: A Retrospective Study
pmc-12567998.creator: Julia Topmöller, Johanna Rieder, Sebastian Meller, Kerstin von Pückler, Holger Volk, Kristina Merhof, Giovanna Bertolini
pmc-12567998.description: Simple SummaryThis study examined adrenal gland size in puppies under one year of age using computed tomography (CT) volumetry and traditional measurements, including length, height, and width. Adrenal volume showed a positive correlation with body weight, highlighting the need for weight-adjusted reference values. Age-related trends and mild asymmetry between the left and right glands were noted.

pmc-12643049.title: Unveiling the Role of circRNAs in Pyroptotic Signalling: From Molecular Crosstalk to Disease Modulation
pmc-12643049.creator: Tengyu Jin, Guodong Xu, Wanru Zhou, Yige Shi, Hebo Wang
pmc-12643049.description: Pyroptosis is a gasdermins‐dependent programmed cell death (PCD) characterised by progressive cellular swelling and plasma membrane rupture (PMR). This process releases intracellular contents that amplify inflammatory cascades and immune activation, involving the pathogenesis of various disorders such as tumours, heart and vascular diseases, diabetic complications and inflammatory/infectious disorders.

pmc-12664147.title: CUEDC1 promotes glycolytic metabolism reprogramming through the CUEDC1/CACNG4/PI3K axis to promote ER-positive breast cancer growth
pmc-12664147.creator: Zexiu Lu, Ming Lei, Jian Chen, Ao Deng, Chao Chang, Jing Chen, Die Meng, Rui Wang, Xueying Wan, Gang Tu, Manran Liu, Lingfeng Tang
pmc-12664147.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe reprogramming of energy metabolism, particularly glycolysis, upholds the malignancy of tumors. The relationship between CUE domain-containing protein-1 (CUEDC1) and glycolysis, along with its influence on the development of estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer (ER+ BRCA), is not well defined.

pmc-13072406.title: Transcriptome Analysis Provides New Insight into Apoptosis and Immunosuppression in Procambarus clarkii After Exposure to High Temperature
pmc-13072406.creator: Shengjie Ren, Wenjing Xu, Xianjun Ma, Qin Gui, Wanqiu Tian, Qiuning Liu, Lishang Dai, Dandan Bian
pmc-13072406.description: Simple SummaryThis study investigates how acute heat stress causes immune failure in farmed red swamp crayfish. Using a 37 °C heat stress model, we found that heat stress increased mortality, disrupted hemocyte balance, and induced severe oxidative stress. Transcriptomic analysis revealed activation of ER stress and autophagy alongside metabolic suppression.

pmc-13156252.title: A call for evidence-based health promotion across the MENA region: From research to impact
pmc-13156252.creator: Haidar Nadrian
pmc-13156252.description: spite significant advances in EBHP in high-income countries, its systematic application remains sporadic and under-prioritized across much of the MENA region. This editorial highlights this critical gap and advocates for a coordinated regional shift toward evidence-informed health promotion. Across MENA countries, health education and promotion (HEHP) research has expanded in volume, yet often remains disconnected from policy impact.

pmc-13632307.title: Neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with worse survival in localized extremity soft tissue sarcoma
pmc-13632307.creator: Brian Benyamini, Riley O’Toole, Mareike Haaren, Joseph Wooley, Dale Shepard, Shauna R. Campbell, Jacob G. Scott, Nathan W. Mesko, Lukas M. Nystrom, Zachary D.C. Burke
pmc-13632307.description: BackgroundThe Area Deprivation Index (ADI) is a validated measure of neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage. This study aimed to assess the association between ADI and long-term (1) disease-specific survival (DSS), (2) metastasis-free survival (MFS), and (3) local recurrence-free survival (RFS) in patients with localized extremity soft tissue sarcoma (STS).
